predictive_observations: The volume burst looked like it was burning out: GeckoTerminal had about $270k volume in the 15-minute window but only $24k in the next 5 minutes, and m5 price was already negative at T2. The unwind the report described happened. Price fell from about $0.000272 at T2 to $0.0000826 at entry (roughly -70%) before the decision time. It kept falling after entry: -20% was touched at 28 minutes, -30% at 34 minutes, and the 60-minute return was -19%.

The bot and bundler counts (352 bundler wallets, 76% bot/degen rate, 0 smart-money signals) fit the pattern of bundled supply being sold into leftover bids. That matches the early drift down after entry and the -26% gross return at 24h.

Burned LP, renounced mint and freeze authority, and a dev balance of 0 correctly ruled out a hard rug. Liquidity never collapsed: the 24h minimum was about $19.4k and the pair was still present at every horizon.

The counterargument proved relevant: a live UAP news cycle plus a fee-routing hook left room for a second leg. Price touched +50% at about 12.0h and +100% at about 12.4h after entry. That was outside the 6h window, and the gain was given back by 24h.
misleading_observations: The report worked from T2-era prices (~$216–260k market cap, 'down ~43% from spike'). By the decision time, market cap was about $79k. Most of the 'fade' had already happened before entry. So the continuation view described a move that was already priced in, not the risk looking forward from entry.

The 'weak' market-feasibility call leaned on a liquidity-to-market-cap ratio of about 18% at T2. At entry the ratio was about 31% ($24.5k / $78.8k), so the structure was less fragile than the report implied.

Calling the token 'coordinated' with a 'fade' call over a 6h window suggested a steady decline. In fact the 6h return was +17% net (+24% gross), and the maximum favorable move within 6h was +36%. The authenticity evidence was probably correct about who drove the first spike, but it said little about the path after a 70% drawdown.
The 4 'renowned' wallets and 740 unique buyers were cited on both sides of the argument. Neither was shown to relate to the outcome.
evidence_that_should_have_changed_conclu: By the decision time, price had fallen about 70% from T2 and about 80% from the ~$431k ATH. The researcher had already pulled a post-T2 DexScreener snapshot and could have re-checked the price. With a drawdown that deep, 'fade' from entry should have been downgraded to neutral or low-confidence.

Pre-entry hourly sigma was about 1.42 (142% per hour). At that volatility, a 6h directional call is mostly noise: neither the 1-sigma nor the 2-sigma barrier was hit in either direction. Medium confidence on a direction was too high given this measurable volatility.
None of this should have flipped the call to 'continue'. The honest answer at the time was a high-variance, roughly symmetric outcome with no rug tail.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: If price has already fallen at least 60% from its intraday ATH by the decision time, 'fade' calls do no better than coin-flip at the 6h horizon. Their 6h return distribution will not differ significantly from neutral calls made under the same drawdown condition.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Pump.fun or PumpSwap tokens less than 24h old. Drawdown from ATH to the decision price is at least 60%. LP is burned or locked. Pre-entry hourly sigma is at least 0.8.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Once bundler and sniper supply has mostly been sold, less inventory is left to press price down. Thin books with fixed AMM liquidity then turn small flows into large moves either way. The directional edge from 'this was a bundled pump' is used up before entry.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: Tokens meeting both of the following conditions will have a negative median 60-minute return from entry, and will touch -20% before +20% more than 55% of the time: (a) bundler-tagged wallets make up at least 50% of GMGN holders, and (b) m5 volume divided by the prior 15-minute volume is at most 0.15 at T2.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: The GMGN bundler count is available. The token has migrated to an AMM. Measured from the decision entry price.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Bundled wallets hold correlated inventory. After the volume burst ends, they keep distributing into a shrinking bid, which pushes price down over the short term whatever the narrative.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: Fee-routing tokens tagged to an unaffiliated public figure who is currently in the news (e.g., via UsePaid) touch +100% from entry within 24h more often than matched bundled tokens without a fee tag, but do not show a higher 24h return.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: The project description names an X handle as the fee recipient. The named figure is in a news cycle dated within 72h. Liquidity at entry is at least $15k and LP is burned.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: A possible claim or post by the named figure acts like a cheap lottery ticket. Traders re-pump the token around news or social moments, but with no lasting holder base the spikes fade back.

structured_output.summary: The report's reading of the spike was good: bot- and bundler-driven, not organic, with no rug risk. The spike collapsed about 70% between T2 and the decision time, so that part was correct, but it happened before entry. Measured from the $79k entry, the path looked like noise from a very volatile token (hourly sigma about 1.4): -19% at 1h, +17% at 6h (the report's own window, which contradicts 'fade'), a touch of +100% at about 12h, then -30% at 24h. The main mistake was anchoring the continuation view and the feasibility assessment on T2 prices instead of the much lower decision-time price, and holding medium confidence on direction despite measurable extreme volatility. Structural checks (burned LP, no dev holdings) held up, and the counterargument about a second leg partly played out. From entry, the outcome was mostly unknowable. The right call would have been neutral or low confidence, not a confident fade.
